findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed category is configured
findings.body: The category lookup assumes the query returns a row, then dereferences `[0]['id']`. If `embed_category` is unset, its value does not match any category (or the setting row is absent), so the migration raises before it can finish. This is a normal configuration and will prevent the upgrade from completing.

findings.title: SELECT row count is checked with cmd_tuples
findings.body: `cmd_tuples` reports rows affected by commands such as INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; for a SELECT it is typically zero. Consequently, even when the legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting contains hosts, this condition skips the inserts, and line 31 then deletes the old settings. The upgrade silently loses the allowlist and leaves embedding disabled.

findings.title: Legacy host values are inserted without normalization
findings.body: The old allowlist accepted host entries containing a scheme or path, but this migration copies each entry verbatim. `record_for_host` later compares the stored value to `URI(...).host`, which contains only the hostname, so migrated entries such as `https://example.com/path` will never match and those sites will lose embed access after upgrade.

findings.title: Configured hosts with ports can never match
findings.body: The model validation accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, and the normalization callback preserves the port. However, `URI(host).host` returns only `example.com`, so this query compares the stored `example.com:8080` against `example.com` and rejects the referer. Any allowed host configured with a port therefore cannot embed.
